comprehensive_feature_film.name: Comprehensive Feature Film (Three-Act)
comprehensive_feature_film.description: A 14-beat structure based on standard Hollywood screenwriting (Save the Cat variant), focusing on character transformation and visual storytelling.
development_questions: What is the central conflict of the story?
What is the theme or message you want to convey?
Who is the protagonist and what is their goal?
Who or what is the antagonist?
What are the major plot points that drive the story forward?
What are the main obstacles the protagonist must overcome?
What is the resolution of the story?
What is at stake for the protagonist if they fail?
What is the protagonist's character flaw or weakness?
scene_questions: What is the goal or purpose of this scene?
What conflict or obstacle does the protagonist face in this scene?
How does this scene advance the plot or develop the characters?
What emotions or themes are explored in this scene?
How does this scene connect to previous and future scenes?
What is the central action or event of this scene?
How does this scene contribute to the overall tone or atmosphere?
What is the resolution or outcome of this scene?
How does this scene foreshadow or set up future events?
How does this scene reveal something new or unexpected?

beats.label: 1. Opening Image
beats.instruction: Introduce the protagonist and their ordinary world. A visual that represents the struggle & tone.

beats.label: 2. Theme Stated
beats.instruction: What your story is about; the message, the truth. Usually spoken to the protagonist.

beats.label: 3. Catalyst
beats.instruction: The event or incident that sets the story in motion. The 'before' world is no more.

beats.label: 4. Debate
beats.instruction: The protagonist considers the situation and decides whether to act. Can I face this challenge?

beats.label: 5. Break into Two
beats.instruction: The protagonist commits to their goal and enters a new world. Leaving the thesis world.

beats.label: 6. B Story
beats.instruction: Introduce the secondary plotline or love interest. Discusses the theme.

beats.label: 7. Fun and Games
beats.instruction: The promise of the premise. The protagonist enjoys some initial success.

beats.label: 8. Midpoint
beats.instruction: A twist or revelation raises the stakes. Everything is 'great' or 'awful'.

beats.label: 9. Bad Guys Close In
beats.instruction: The antagonist gains the upper hand and puts pressure on the protagonist.

beats.label: 10. All is Lost
beats.instruction: The protagonist suffers a major setback. Something or someone dies (literal or metaphorical).

beats.label: 11. Dark Night of the Soul
beats.instruction: The protagonist confronts their character flaw and questions their ability to succeed.

beats.label: 12. Break into Three
beats.instruction: The protagonist regains their focus and commits to a new plan (Synthesis).

beats.label: 13. Finale
beats.instruction: The protagonist faces the antagonist in a final showdown.

beats.label: 14. Final Image
beats.instruction: The story concludes with a final image that mirrors the opening image, showing change.

beats.label: 1. Ordinary World
beats.instruction: Establish the Status Quo. Show the hero's lack or flaw.

beats.label: 2. Call to Adventure
beats.instruction: The Inciting Incident. A disruption to the Ordinary World.

beats.label: 3. Refusal of Call
beats.instruction: The Hero hesitates due to fear or insecurity.

beats.label: 4. Mentor
beats.instruction: The Hero meets a guide who provides tools or wisdom.

beats.label: 5. Crossing Threshold
beats.instruction: The Point of No Return. Entering the Special World.

beats.label: 6. Tests, Allies, Enemies
beats.instruction: Exploring the new world, learning rules, meeting the team.

beats.label: 7. Approach
beats.instruction: Preparation for the main crisis. Deepening relationships.

beats.label: 8. Ordeal
beats.instruction: The central crisis. Death and Rebirth. Facing the greatest fear.

beats.label: 9. Reward
beats.instruction: Seizing the Sword. The Hero gains the object of their quest.

beats.label: 10. Road Back
beats.instruction: The consequences of the Act. The chase/escape.

beats.label: 11. Resurrection
beats.instruction: The Final Exam. The Hero proves they have changed.

beats.label: 12. Return
beats.instruction: Returning home with the Elixir to heal the Ordinary World.

beats.label: 1. Introduction
beats.instruction: Establish characters and setting.

beats.label: 2. Rising Action
beats.instruction: Conflict is introduced and tension builds.

beats.label: 3. Climax
beats.instruction: The turning point. The point of highest tension.

beats.label: 4. Falling Action
beats.instruction: The conflict unravels, leading towards the inevitable.

beats.label: 5. Catastrophe
beats.instruction: The tragic conclusion. The hero's failure or demise.

beats.label: 1. The Hook
beats.instruction: The starting state. Opposite of the ending.

beats.label: 2. Plot Point 1
beats.instruction: The Call to Adventure. Life changes.

beats.label: 3. Pinch Point 1
beats.instruction: Pressure is applied. The antagonist strikes.

beats.label: 4. Midpoint
beats.instruction: The hero shifts from reactive to active.

beats.label: 5. Pinch Point 2
beats.instruction: The jaws of defeat. All hope seems lost.

beats.label: 6. Plot Point 2
beats.instruction: The solution is found. The hero has the key.

beats.label: 7. Resolution
beats.instruction: The conflict is resolved. The new normal.
